data.narrative:
Until, a Series A-stage biotech company founded by Laura Deming and Hunter Davis, has raised $106M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparative set of 3 public peers (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) and 8 private frontier biotech companies, though narrow peer matching within identical stage and valuation tier proved limited.

Of three valuation methods examined, only stage-progression proved applicable. This method uses the $106M total capital raised as a proxy for current enterprise value and applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A-to-next-stage progression in biotech, yielding $212M. The peer-median approach could not be executed: while 7 same-sector peers exist, none of the 0 same-stage and 0 adjacent-stage peers satisfied the minimum threshold of 3 comparable datapoints. Public-comp anchoring was inapplicable due to absence of revenue disclosure, standard for private companies. The median of public Biotech & Health peers stands at 8.1x P/S, but lacks actionable application here.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $180M to $244M, with a median of $212M. This narrow range reflects reliance on a single method. Key uncertainties include Until's actual revenue trajectory, capital efficiency relative to peer cohorts, and stage-specific multiplier volatility in frontier biotech. Investors should prioritize obtaining revenue, burn rate, and clinical progress data to refine this estimate.
